original.target_description: Experiment 2: Self-promoters' versus recipients' perceptions of recipients' anger. Matching named emotion-specific reporter contrast in the covariate-adjusted mixed ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Participants; analytic model N unverified. Completion/recruitment count 154 is separate from the candidate retained count 151.
n.exclusions: Three excluded responses: two self-promoters, one recipient; two denied ever bragging and one did not provide a self-promotion instance.
n.location: Accepted manuscript pp. 13–14, Experiment 2 Method and Results
n.quote:
One hundred and fifty-four Amazon

Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers (Mage = 30.86, SD = 11.19; 37.3% female) accessed and

completed a short study on personality ... Responses from three participants (two in the self-promoter and one in the recipient

condition) were excluded because two participants claimed that they had never bragged in their

life, and the other participant did not describe a self-promotion instance but only indicated s/he

used to have a friend who was a braggart. ... We conducted a two-way mixed ANOVA on the seven

emotional reactions with the reporter (self-promoter vs. recipient) condition as between subject

factor, the emotions as within subject factors, and the topic dummies as covariates (the topic

‘luck’ served as baseline).

notes: Identity independently checked from repository cover and manuscript title page: Irene Scopelliti, George Loewenstein, Joachim Vosgerau; matching title (with subtitle Miscalibrated Predictions of Emotional Responses to Self-Promotion), Psychological Science 26(6), 903–914, DOI 10.1177/0956797615573516. Supplied text is an accepted primary manuscript with methods, results and references, not an abstract or secondary article. No PDF supplied; no rendering possible within assigned sources. Manuscript pages 13–15 contain Experiment 2; the input p. 6 locator appears to refer to another pagination. The source reports 154 workers completed the study and three responses were excluded. Candidate retained participant count is 154 - 3 = 151. It does not explicitly print the critical-model analytic N or counts of mutually exclusive final reporter groups; recruitment/completion minus exclusions is not promoted to an explicit model N. No N inferred from degrees of freedom. Excluded: two self-promoters and one recipient (two never bragged; one described a braggart friend rather than a self-promotion instance). Only assigned unfinished fields examined; other fields are placeholders.
